classification.difficultyReason: Infer derivative signs, zeros, relative gradient sizes and limiting behaviour from nine qualitative curves, including vertical tangents and asymptotes.

content.prompt: Sketch the derivative function for each curve.

spec.description: Symmetric rounded bell above the x-axis, with a maximum on the y-axis and two flattening tails.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative function: increasing for x<0, stationary at x=0, decreasing for x>0; outer gradients tend to zero. No equation or numerical scale is supplied.

answer.short: Positive for $x<0$, zero at $x=0$, negative for $x>0$; both tails approach zero. See sketch.
answer.worked: The curve increases to its maximum at $x=0$, then decreases. Therefore $f'(x)>0$ to the left, $f'(0)=0$ and $f'(x)<0$ to the right. The slope first becomes steeper and then flatter on each side, giving a positive left lobe and a negative right lobe. Both tails approach the $x$-axis.

spec.description: Positive left lobe and negative right lobe, crossing at the origin, with tails approaching zero.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative derivative; no numerical vertical scale.

spec.description: Flattening negative left tail, local minimum left of zero, steep rise through the origin, local maximum right of zero, flattening positive right tail.
spec.mathematics: Two stationary points; gradient negative, positive, negative in consecutive intervals. No equation or numerical scale is supplied.

answer.short: Negative, then positive, then negative, with zeros beneath the two turning points. The central positive peak is between shallow negative outer lobes.
answer.worked: Mark zeros of $f'$ at the local minimum and local maximum of $f$. The original curve decreases, then increases, then decreases, so the derivative has signs $-,+,-$. Its greatest positive value occurs near the steep central rise. The outer negative gradients approach zero.

spec.description: Tall positive central peak, zeros aligned with the original turning points, shallow negative outer lobes and tails approaching zero from below.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative derivative; zeros use the same horizontal positions as the given turning points.

spec.description: Two positive symmetric branches, approaching the x-axis away from zero and rising unboundedly towards the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: Increasing on x<0 and decreasing on x>0; undefined at x=0. No formula is specified.

answer.short: Positive on $x<0$ and negative on $x>0$; undefined at $x=0$. Each outer tail approaches zero.
answer.worked: The left branch rises increasingly steeply towards $x=0$, so its derivative is positive and grows without bound. The right branch falls steeply from near $x=0$ and then flattens, so its derivative is negative and approaches zero. Keep the two derivative branches separate at $x=0$.

spec.description: Positive left branch and negative right branch with vertical asymptote x=0 and horizontal asymptote y=0.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative derivative signs and limiting behaviour; neither branch crosses an axis.

spec.description: Symmetric bell with maximum (0,1), crossing the x-axis twice and approaching dashed y=-1 from above.
spec.mathematics: Maximum at x=0, horizontal asymptote y=-1. The horizontal locations of the x-intercepts are unspecified.

answer.short: Positive left lobe, zero at the origin, negative right lobe; both tails approach zero.
answer.worked: The original curve increases for $x<0$, has a horizontal tangent at $x=0$ and decreases for $x>0$. Thus the derivative is positive, zero and negative respectively. The original curve flattens towards its horizontal asymptote at both ends, so the derivative approaches zero.

spec.description: Positive left lobe and negative right lobe crossing the origin, flattening towards the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Derivative sign pattern +,0,-; horizontal asymptote y=0.

spec.description: Symmetric trough with minimum at the origin, approaching the dashed horizontal asymptote y=1 from below.
spec.mathematics: Decreasing on x<0, stationary at x=0, increasing on x>0; horizontal asymptote y=1.

answer.short: Negative left lobe, zero at the origin, positive right lobe; both tails approach zero.
answer.worked: The original curve decreases to a horizontal tangent at the origin, then increases. Hence $f'$ is negative for $x<0$, zero at $x=0$ and positive for $x>0$. On each side the slope becomes steepest before flattening towards the asymptote, producing the two lobes shown.

spec.description: Negative left lobe and positive right lobe crossing the origin, with tails approaching zero.
spec.mathematics: Derivative sign pattern -,0,+; horizontal asymptote y=0.

spec.description: First-quadrant decreasing concave-up branch, unbounded near x=0 and flattening towards the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Domain x>0, negative gradient increasing towards zero; no function equation is supplied.

answer.short: For $x>0$, a negative increasing curve approaching zero from below, with $f'(x)\to-\infty$ as $x\to0^+$.
answer.worked: The original curve decreases everywhere, so its derivative is negative. Its downward slope is extremely steep near $x=0$ and becomes progressively flatter as $x$ increases. Sketch a derivative below the $x$-axis, rising from unbounded negative values towards zero.

spec.description: Negative branch on x>0, tending downwards near the y-axis and towards zero from below to the right.
spec.mathematics: f'<0, increasing towards zero, with vertical asymptote x=0.

spec.description: Increasing concave-down curve starting at the origin with a vertical tangent, becoming flatter to the right.
spec.mathematics: Nonnegative original domain; derivative positive on x>0 and unbounded near the endpoint. No equation is printed.

answer.short: For $x>0$, a positive decreasing curve tending to $+\infty$ near zero and towards zero to the right.
answer.worked: The original curve increases, so $f'(x)>0$ for $x>0$. Its slope decreases as the curve flattens. The vertical tangent at the origin corresponds to an unbounded positive derivative as $x\to0^+$; there is no finite derivative at the endpoint.

spec.description: Positive decreasing branch on x>0, unbounded near zero and approaching the x-axis to the right.
spec.mathematics: Positive derivative decreasing towards zero; no finite value at x=0.

spec.description: Increasing concave-down branch on x>0, descending without bound near the y-axis and crossing at (1,0).
spec.mathematics: Positive decreasing gradients, vertical asymptote x=0 and x-intercept 1. No formula is printed.

answer.short: For $x>0$, a positive decreasing curve tending to $+\infty$ near zero and towards zero to the right.
answer.worked: The original curve increases throughout its domain, so its derivative stays positive. It is very steep near $x=0$ and becomes progressively flatter, so the derivative decreases from unbounded positive values towards zero. The original $x$-intercept at $1$ is not a zero of the derivative because the tangent there is not horizontal.

spec.description: Positive decreasing branch on x>0 with the coordinate axes as asymptotes.
spec.mathematics: Derivative positive and tending to zero to the right; unbounded near x=0.

spec.description: Upper unit semicircle with labelled endpoints -1 and 1 and labelled maximum height 1.
spec.mathematics: Upper half of x^2+y^2=1, from (-1,0) to (1,0), maximum (0,1). Equal coordinate units retain the semicircle.

answer.short: A decreasing curve on $-1<x<1$, through the origin, with vertical asymptotes $x=-1$ and $x=1$; positive on the left and negative on the right.
answer.worked: The semicircle rises on $-1<x<0$, has a horizontal tangent at $x=0$ and falls on $0<x<1$. Hence $f'$ is positive, zero and negative respectively. The tangent slope decreases throughout. Near $x=-1$ it becomes unboundedly positive; near $x=1$ it becomes unboundedly negative. Sketch only between these two vertical asymptotes.

spec.description: Decreasing curve through the origin between labelled dashed vertical asymptotes x=-1 and x=1.
spec.mathematics: Derivative of the upper unit semicircle, plotted as -x/sqrt(1-x^2) on -1<x<1. The formula is used only to reconstruct the figure; the worked method remains graphical.
